evidence.quote: | Ready, Some books when Transfer.holdsRecords books ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule is in Tier 2. Summa.Storage.Transfer holds the file format, the refusal checks and their order, the data-version match and the 'new books only' predicate. The engine (Summa.Web.Engine) holds the Settings-page transitions: the GitHub refusal, the files-pack check and import-or-refuse, and it calls Transfer for each decision. The only Tier 3 change maps the three kernel event names to engine messages, with no logic. The HTML only binds events and view values.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect below Tier 4. The time comes in through the message context (ctx.Now) and is passed to the pure Transfer.export. The download and the save are returned as effect data (OfferDownload, and SaveBooks via the existing `save`) for the edge to perform. Base64 and UTF-8 encoding are pure. Transfer.fs uses no I/O, clock or console symbols.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Most facts come from one source: the schema and version are literals in Transfer, the classification is Exports.Classification, the data version is Exports.dataVersion, the snapshot is LocalSnapshot.encode/decode and dates use Codec.dateText. One fact is restated, though: the exportedAt timestamp format is written as two separate string literals, one for writing (stamp) and one for parsing (exportedAtOf). The copies agree, but nothing keeps them together.

evidence.quote: elif n <> 1m && contentsOf value <> Some(contents restored.Books) then

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new rules are in Tier 2: the definition of the counts, the contents check, the accepted versions and the preview wording. The engine's preview calls Transfer.read and Transfer.contents rather than counting records itself. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code decides anything; the HTML only binds booksTransferPreview.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect. The preview is a pure function of the pasted text, computed in the engine transition. The contents check in Transfer.read is pure. No clock, I/O or port changes are involved.

evidence.quote: | Ok(Json.Number n) when n <> 1m && n <> decimal Version -> Error
elif n <> 1m && contentsOf value <> Some(contents restored.Books) then
Notice = Some $"Books imported from a transfer file exported on {Codec.dateText (DateOnly.FromDateTime transferred.ExportedAt.UtcDateTime)}."

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one definition (Transfer.contents), used by the export, the check and the preview. Some facts are restated, though. The legacy version 1 is a bare literal `1m` written twice, next to the named Version constant. The rule for the export's UTC date is written inline in both the preview and the import notice. The copies agree today, but none of them points to one shared definition.
